messages:
Marta: Heads up — ran the escalation-sim on prod alerts for the last 30d to compare paging vs ticketing outcomes. TL;DR: short mute windows (<=5m) still produce too many pages for GPU flares, we need smarter grouping and a noise-aware policy.
Devon: nice, do you have the numbers?
Marta: Yes — quick summary: noise_fraction (alerts that resolved <10m) = 0.37. If we classify any alert with >20% noise as ticket-only we reduce pages by ~48% but MTTR for true incidents goes up ~12%.
Alex: can you share how you simulated that?
Marta: sent over the script to the infra bucket; high level: replayed alert stream, applied different mute windows and grouping strategies, measured page count, duplicate factor, and whether a subsequent higher-sev alert occurred within 30m. key knobs:
```
# promql used to compute short-lived alerts
sum by (alertname) (increase(ALERTS{severity="warning"}[10m])) / sum by (alertname) (increase(ALERTS[30d]))
```
and a pseudo-rule for dynamic mute: 
```
if cardinality(node) > 3 then ticket
else if unstable_count(node) > 2 then page with 2m mute
else page with 30s mute
```
Devon: grouping by node_pool/region helped?
Marta: yes — group_by(node_pool, region) removed ~30% duplicate pages caused by single-update storms when a pool controller churns nodes. grouping by job/instance was too noisy because of ephemeral pods.
Priya: any cost implications? fewer pages = fewer oncall interruptions but also more tickets = more async ops. Did you model pager duty costs vs incident cost?
Marta: rough calc: pages down 48% -> ~200 fewer page-hours per month. If an actual incident has 12% longer MTTR, estimated cloud-sla cost increase is ~1.6% (depends on workload). Net ops time saved > cloud cost delta for most scenarios.
AlertBot: AlertSimBot: analysis finished — processed 72,423 alerts, sample size 12 clusters.
Devon: risk: long mute windows might hide cascading failures where one node flapping becomes cluster-wide after 8-12m.
Marta: agreed. Proposed compromise: dynamic policy keyed off cardinality and escalation hazard score. heuristics we used: 
- if distinct nodes affected >= 4 within 10m -> immediate page (high hazard)
- else if noise_fraction > 0.25 and distinct_nodes == 1 -> ticket with 1h mute
- else use short-page (30s) with 2m cooldown
This preserves pages for multi-node problems while reducing noise from single-node flares.
Alex: can you push a PR? would like to review the Prometheus rule diffs and a Grafana panel showing post-change page-rate trend.
Marta: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-alerts/pull/482 — includes Prometheus rules, a new Grafana 'page vs ticket' panel, and the simulation notebook.
Priya: can we soft-roll: route simulated pages to #ops-ticketing for 48h (so ops gets used to new behavior but it doesn't wake everyone)?
Devon: sounds good. also add a runbook blurb about what to do if we see a spike after change.
Marta: will add runbook and schedule a 30m sync Thursday 10:00am PT. tagging @devon @alex @priya to join.
Alex: :thumbsup:
Priya: :thumbsup:
Devon: thanks, good approach.
Marta: I'll post the experiment results (raw CSV + notebook) in the thread after the sync.
